title: Proposal for Mandatory Child-proof Pool Fences at Private Swimming Pools
what_it_is: Proposal for Mandatory Child-proof Pool Fences at Private Swimming Pools

sections.label: Private pool safety measures
sections.summary: BCA has guidelines on warning signs, flooring, depth markings and lighting, and private pool owners can install child-resistant barriers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether BCA has plans to mandate child-proof pool fences in private swimming pools in view of the increasing number of near-drowning cases involving children and 10 deaths reported in KK Women's and Children's Hospital from 2011 to 2015; and (b) what are the measures taken by BCA over the years to improve the safety of private swimming pools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: There are also safety-related guidelines under the Code for warning signs, slip-resistant flooring, depth markings as well as providing adequate lighting.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: As an added safety precaution, private pool owners can install child-resistant barriers, and for strata-titled developments, the management corporations may make such improvements to their swimming pools, by passing a special resolution.

sections.label: Primary school water safety
sections.summary: All primary school students are taught water safety knowledge and basic swimming skills through the SwimSafer 2.0 programme with SportSG.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: As part of the physical education curriculum, all primary school students are taught water safety knowledge and basic swimming skills.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: This is done through the SwimSafer 2.0 programme, in partnership with SportSG.

sections.label: Adult supervision for pool safety
sections.summary: A child restraint barrier would not have been sufficient in the mentioned cases, and adult supervision is the most effective means.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: It is unclear for the others how the situation occurred.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: But in those cases that I mentioned, the provision of a child restraint barrier, even if mandated, would not have been sufficient in avoiding these incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: What is important then would be adult supervision, which is still the most effective means in ensuring the safety of young children when they use the pool.

sections.label: Barriers by resolution review
sections.summary: Management corporations and condominium owners could pass a resolution to put barriers in place, which could be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Today, even without a mandatory requirement, Management Corporation Strata Titles and condominium owners could potentially pass a resolution to put barriers in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Having said that, it could be something we can review.
